At one time I did a lot of work helping other people find work - I don't know why I am suddenly thinking about it this morning, but I thought I would share this useful information.

Looking for a job is at times tedious and disheartening - rejection is bad for moral, and it is easy to become discouraged, especially when it seems there is no work out there to be found.

This is the point I wish to discuss - there is always - ALWAYS - work to found. People die, they take sick leave, they retire, they move away, they get fired, they quit. The simple fact is there are new job openings created every single day - no matter how bad the economy gets. Even in the worst depressions, new job openings are happening. It may not be exactly the work you are looking for - but work is there if you will have it.

In a tough job market, the average person will try to find work - they will put out 50, even 100 resumes, and then, more often than not, if they are unsuccessful, they will then stop looking. The difference between the successful candidate and these people is you do not stop looking - you keep on that motherfucker until you get that job. Period. It's as simple as that.

There is something else you need to know - if you are being continuously rejected, it is likely in part because you are failing to present yourself properly. There is help available locally to improve that situation if that is the case - ask at The United Way for a referral - they know who does it locally.

As a former employer, I can tell you that every employer is always looking for good talent. Good workers are damned hard to find - and when you think you have a chance to get a good one, employers will bend over backwards to find a way to make that happen. They will even lay off somebody on the shit list to make room for you. It's ruthless, I know - but it is what it is. Good employees are good for the bottom line. Good companies are all about good employees first.

You have to talk to people - you have to network - you have to be seen as a person, with a name, and a situation - not another unknown resume. Ask for help - from everyone you know and meet. The majority of job openings are never advertised at all. It goes by word of mouth and referral.

Don't like the job you are in now? - need a raise and can't get it? - do exactly the same thing - go get a new job - then leave the one you are at. The power to write your own ticket is already in your hands.

Advice for life, not just finding a job. You can go as far as you're willing to work. Put in the time, never give up:

The power to write your own ticket is already in your hands.

Economics - sometime you take a job just to get the cash flowing again - but keep on looking for the right job at the same time - and in extreme situations you might consider starting your own business doing your dream job - start it as a part time hobby business - and let it grow from there.

My best business actually started in a similar way - I was in school and started a company to get some extra part time money on the side - then the phone started ringing in a major way - that turned into a ten year multi-million dollar operation. I had no intention for it to happen that way. It was completely by accident - but it also allowed me to do exactly what I wanted to do, and get paid to do it.

As for the long term unemployment problems - the truth is that most people have a different image of themselves in their own minds than what is the actual image everyone else sees. I mean literally 99% of people live this way. People do not actually know how they are coming across to others - and more often than not there is something wrong that they are unaware of.

Now, the best way to fix this is through professional consultation with employment counselors, (I used to be one.) Our best trick was the video tape exercise. We have the client do a recorded interview - then play that back so the client can see it for themselves. I did that exercise myself, and the results were quite shocking to me. An eye opener to be sure, but it also got me to correct aspects of my professional personality that led to a dramatic performance improvement, and later wage increases and promotion.

This is called employment counseling, and it is freely available usually through local private charities - again, the United Way is an umbrella organization for all smaller charities - so they know exactly who is providing this service locally. You can also pay to get the corporate version of what is exactly the same training - but it will cost you thousands of dollars. The training itself comes out of the schools of psychology and sociology - and is part of the Human Resources field of study - and it overlaps into the world of sales - psychology of persuasion - because what you are really doing is selling yourself and your skills. Proper presentation makes all the difference.

Also - sorry I missed part of your question - long term gaps in the employment record. That's a little harder - especially if you were in jail or something... there are ways to work around that too - but essentially if you were not in the employment market it is best if you have a reason for that - sometimes you have to work a little harder to avoid that area in an interview - sometimes employers will look past that because they like other stuff they see. The past can be outweighed by present circumstance - and again, counselors can help you with that as well. In practice we never had a problem getting past that issue.

It is also important to understand that this situation is far more common than most people realize. Interviewers see it all of the time because most people do actually go through that. Interviewers are not just looking for the ideal candidate - they are also on the watch for problem areas - things like drugs - general criminal activity - laziness, even insanity:) Believe it or not - there are employers out there who prefer to hire criminals. Just like there are employers who seek the lazy. There's a place for stupid people too. There is room for almost everybody. (almost.)

It really comes down to fitting you correctly into a job that suits your individual personality and situation - and trained professionals are available who specialize in doing just that, working one on one with you - because, it is not enough for you to just have a job, it also has to be a job that ideally you enjoy doing, or at the very least can tolerate.

Furthermore - look at it from the interviewer's position - we have you, Candidate A who meets the current qualifications - but has this gap area on the resume - and your explanation about that was a little vague as you danced around the issue. So that is that.

Candidate B also meets the qualifications - and he left his other job only two weeks ago - but WHY? You call over there and get a good reference - but does that really mean anything? No serious employer will give you a bad reference without a well documented case because you can and do get sued for that - even if the employer is in the right he may still lose time and money - better to offload the troublesome employee onto your competitor and then he is their problem and you are now rid of that prick.

See the interviewer's problem? A vaguely explained gap is sometimes not as threatening as another possible threat - and in the end it comes down to the interviewer's own mind - and perhaps how well the rest of your interview went. I assume you will be otherwise charming and can also get some people to vouch for your character.
